But the historic milestone arrives amid political instability and skepticism among ordinary people fueled by fears of price rises. Story by Luke Shrago.

summary: Five years ago, the United Kingdom left the single European market after a post-Brexit transition. title: Bulgaria bids farewell to lev currency, awaits euro adoption amid inflation concerns
summary: Bulgaria will formally adopt the euro as its currency starting on January 1, leaving behind the lev, which it has used since the late 19th century. The move is unpopular with almost half the country's population over fears it could spark higher inflation, something that mistrusted authorities have been trying to downplay. title: Russia says 'no evidence needed' to accuse Ukraine of drone attack on Putin's residence
summary: Ukraine said Tuesday there was no "plausible" evidence it launched a drone attack on one of Russian President Vladimir Putin's residences, and accused Moscow of peddling falsehoods to influence peace talks. Story by Laurent Berstecher.

title: Germany: Thieves break in to thousands of safes, stealing 30 million euros
summary: Robbers used a large drill to break into a German savings bank's vault room and steal cash, gold and jewelry worth some €30 million ($35 million), police said Tuesday. While the criminals remained at large, hundreds of distressed bank customers massed outside the branch on Tuesday demanding information, but were kept at bay by police. Story by Eliza Herbert…

title: Gaza: Some Palestinians turn to art to process war trauma
summary: In Gaza, a fragile ceasefire has been in place since October, but humanitarian conditions remain dire. Many in the international community accuse Israel of refusing to allow necessary aid into the territory. In this difficult context, some Palestinians are turning to art to help them process the trauma of the war. Story by Ellen Gainsford and Loïc Chalavon.

title: Train crash on Peru's Machu Picchu line kills one and injures 40
summary: A head-on collision between two trains on the line that services Peru's Machu Picchu killed one person and injured at least 40 others, authorities said, updating an earlier toll. The deceased was the conductor of one of the two trains, according to the prosecutor's office in Cusco, the city closest to the famous Inca citadel. Story by Oliver Farry.

summary: When the MetroCard replaced the New York City subway token in 1994, the swipeable plastic card infused much-needed modernity into one of the world’s oldest and largest transit systems. summary: A video of a protester sitting in the street and facing down police on motorbikes during demonstrations that erupted in Tehran in recent days has gone viral on social media, with some observers calling it Iran's "Tiananmen moment". title: Saudi Arabia bombs Yemen city of Mukalla over weapons shipment from UAE for separatists
summary: Saudi Arabia bombed Yemen's port city of Mukalla on Tuesday after a weapons shipment from the United Arab Emirates arrived for separatist forces in the war-torn country, and warned that it viewed Emirati actions as “extremely dangerous.” Story by Ellen Gainsford.

title: Iran to unleash 'decisive' response if economic protests destabilise country, prosecutor says
summary: Iran will meet any attempt to use ongoing protests driven by economic hardship to foment insecurity with a "decisive response", prosecutor-general Mohammad Movahedi-Azad said Wednesday. Shopkeeper-led demonstrations broke out Sunday to protest the sanction-hit country's rising cost of living.

title: Taiwan coastguard says Chinese ships 'withdrawing' after drills
summary: Chinese warships and coastguard vessels are withdrawing from waters around Taiwan, the island's coastguard said Wednesday, with Beijing's military drills appearing to be "over".

summary: An overnight Russian drone attack on Ukraine's Black Sea port of Odesa wounded at least four people, three of them children, Ukrainian authorities said Wednesday. title: AFCON: Senegal beat Benin and finish top of their group
summary: Senegal beat Benin 3-0 and qualified for the AFCON round of 16 as group winners ahead of DR Congo.

title: From science to sport: These are the stories that lifted spirits in 2025
summary: Amid conflicts and crises, 2025 also brought reasons for optimism, medical breakthroughs, encouraging signs for the planet and sporting and cultural surprises. As the world heads into 2026, FRANCE 24 looks back at some of the stories that offered moments of relief.

title: Thailand releases 18 Cambodian soldiers held prisoner since July border clashes
summary: Thailand released 18 Cambodian soldiers held prisoner since border clashes broke out between the two countries in July as part of a renewed ceasefire signed Saturday. Dozens of people have been killed and more than a million more driven from their homes after renewed fighting erupted in December.

title: The Bright Side: Libyans savour shared heritage as national museum reopens after 14 years
summary: For the first time since the outbreak of civil war in 2011, Libyans are reconnecting with their ancient heritage at the recently reopened national museum in Tripoli.

title: Guinea coup leader Doumbouya elected president in provisional results
summary: More than three years after taking power in a military coup, Guinea’s junta leader Mamady Doumbouya secured a sweeping election victory on Tuesday that cements his grip on the presidency, in a vote critics say was held in a tightly controlled political environment as the country seeks to draw a line under years of upheaval.

title: Congo president Sassou Nguesso to seek re-election in March 2026
summary: Congo is heading towards another tightly watched presidential race after the ruling Congolese Labour Party confirmed it will again back veteran leader Denis Sassou Nguesso, extending the 82-year-old’s decades-long grip on power into a 2026 election already drawing opposition scrutiny.

title: MH370 search resumes in Indian Ocean nearly 12 years after plane's disappearance
summary: Nearly 12 years after Malaysia Airlines flight MH370 vanished with 239 people on board, a renewed search has begun in the remote southern Indian Ocean, as investigators deploy advanced deep-sea technology in a fresh bid to solve one of aviation’s most enduring mysteries.

title: Syria arrests suspects in Latakia after sectarian violence, curfew imposed
summary: Syrian authorities have arrested 21 people in the coastal province of Latakia over alleged links to the ousted government of Bashar al-Assad, state media reported, after sectarian violence prompted an overnight curfew in the provincial capital.

title: AFCON 2025: Nigeria complete near-perfect group stage with third straight win
summary: Nigeria have completed a near-perfect group stage after claiming a third straight win by beating Uganda 3-1.

title: Situation in Gaza is 'catastrophic’, foreign ministers from 10 countries warn
summary: A group of 10 countries, including France, warned on Tuesday that the situation in Gaza was "catastrophic" due to the "renewed deterioration of the humanitarian situation" in the Palestinian enclave. They called on Israel to allow greater access for NGOs and to lift restrictions on importing essential medical and shelter equipment.

title: Turkey arrests 357 people in operation against Islamic State group
summary: Turkey said it arrested 357 people on Tuesday linked to the Islamic State group, following intelligence reports that the terrorist organisation was "planning attacks" during Christmas and New Year.

title: Why China is bringing out the big guns for military drills around Taiwan
summary: China stepped up its military drills around Taiwan with live-fire exercises on Tuesday, the second day of an operation dubbed “Justice Mission 2025". The massive show of force comes at a crucial time as Beijing seeks to capitalise on domestic political tensions in Taiwan and issue a warning to foreign powers supporting Taipei.
